steps.description:
A variable is used to store a value that can be reused and updated throughout a program. This simple yet powerful concept enables programmers to move beyond writing small, rigid scripts to building large, dynamic, and scalable programs.
This is how you create a variable.

Once a variable is created, it will show up in menu.

This is how you set or modify a variable's value.

   

You can display the variable value but remember to use Create-text-with block to convert it to text for display.
 

We are going to create our first variable and test it.
  1. Create a variable and name it IDK.
  2. Set its value to 1.
  3. Display the variable on the LCD for 1 second.
  4. Increase the variable by 2.
  5. Display the variable on the LCD for 1 second again.
  6. Repeat Step(4) to Step(5) five times and observe the results. Did you see 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 appearing in order?

This is how you create a variable.

Once a variable is created, it will show up in menu.

This is how you set or modify a variable's value.

   

You can display the variable value but remember to use Create-text-with block to convert it to text for display.
 

You can use a variable to control the value of a block by plugging it in as shown.

    


Although it is fun to give our variable a random name, we should name it meaningfully (usually indicating what it stores). 

Create a variable and name it column. Use it to control the LCD column to display "X" as shown.

This is how you create a variable.

Once a variable is created, it will show up in menu.

This is how you set or modify a variable's value.

   

You can display the variable value but remember to use Create-text-with block to convert it to text for display.
 

You can use a variable to control the value of a block by plugging it in as shown.

    


Although it is fun to give our variable a random name, we should name it meaningfully (usually indicating what it stores). 

Create a variable column and use it to control the LCD column. Display the animation as shown. The character moves a space every second.

Use Repeat loop to keep adjusting the column.

Variables are super useful, and most programs need more than just one to get things working.
This is how you set or modify a variable's value.

   

You can display the variable value but remember to use Create-text-with block to convert it to text for display.
 

You can use two variables to control the position of text on the LCD: one for the column and one for the row.

You can check a variable value as shown below.

      

In the previous step, you made an 'X' move from left to right. Now, let’s add a twist, make it bounce!

Load the code in your previous step. Create another variable to control the row. As the 'X' moves a space, toggle the row between 0 and 1.

You may need to use the If block to toggle the row between 0 and 1.
